text: Which ticket will win the 2026 FIDE presidential election?
The Jan Henric Buettner and Malcolm Pein ticket wins the 2026 FIDE presidential election.
The Wadim Rosenstein and Gordon Tang ticket wins the 2026 FIDE presidential election.
The Timur Turlov and Viswanathan Anand ticket wins the 2026 FIDE presidential election.
A ticket other than Buettner/Pein, Rosenstein/Tang and Turlov/Anand wins the 2026 FIDE presidential election.
Gordon Tang has pledged substantial personal financial backing to the Rosenstein-Tang campaign for the 2026 FIDE presidential election.
Incumbent FIDE president Arkady Dvorkovich, backed by most national federation votes in the 2022 election, is seeking re-election in 2026.
Timur Turlov has pledged substantial personal financial resources to fund his 2026 FIDE presidential campaign.
Timur Turlov lacks prior experience holding an official position within FIDE or national chess federation leadership before the 2026 election cycle.
Jan Henric Buettner has publicly financed his campaign with personal wealth, funding initiatives such as increased prize funds for FIDE events.
Arkady Dvorkovich led the incumbent FIDE administration with the backing of most national federation voting blocs as of 2026.
Incumbent FIDE president Arkady Dvorkovich had not publicly ruled out seeking re-election as of September 2026.

FIDE presidential election rules require candidate tickets to be nominated by member federations well before the 2026 congress, and only Buettner/Pein, Rosenstein/Tang and Turlov/Anand had secured sufficient federation backing as of September 2026.
Jan Henric Buettner’s entrepreneurial background gives the Buettner–Pein ticket substantial experience in organizational leadership and international business.
Jan Henric Buettner lacked prior elected leadership experience within FIDE or a national chess federation as of 2026.
Viswanathan Anand is a five-time world chess champion with global name recognition among national chess federations.
FIDE's voting members are national chess federations rather than individual chess players.
FIDE's 2026 nomination deadline had not passed as of September 2026.
Wadim Rosenstein secured public endorsements from multiple national chess federation leaders for the 2026 FIDE presidential election.
Wadim Rosenstein has never held an elected position within FIDE as of September 2026.
Jan Henric Buettner co-founded and funded the Freestyle Chess Grand Slam tour, which offers prize funds exceeding those of many traditional FIDE-sanctioned events.
FIDE electoral rules prohibit candidates from directly offering financial inducements to national federations in exchange for votes.
Arkady Dvorkovich won re-election as FIDE President in 2022 with support from a majority of national federations.
Several national federations that backed Arkady Dvorkovich in the 2022 election publicly announced support for a rival ticket ahead of the 2026 vote.
An incumbent FIDE administration with majority federation voting bloc support typically wins re-election in FIDE presidential elections.
National federation voting bloc support prior to a FIDE election does not guarantee delivery of votes in the final election ballot.
Increased prize funds and well-financed campaigns attract more FIDE federation votes in FIDE presidential elections.
Personal wealth spending by FIDE presidential candidates in prior elections, such as Kirsan Ilyumzhinov's era, has not consistently determined FIDE electoral outcomes.
Additional FIDE presidential tickets beyond Buettner/Pein, Rosenstein/Tang and Turlov/Anand formed after nominations closed in previous FIDE election cycles.
Viswanathan Anand has served as a FIDE Deputy President since 2022, giving the ticket an incumbent-adjacent standing within FIDE's governing structure.
Arkady Dvorkovich's incumbent network of national federation officials backed his re-election bids in both the 2018 and 2022 FIDE presidential elections.
Gordon Tang built extensive networks among Asian national chess federations through prior business and philanthropic activities before 2026.
Gordon Tang has no prior record of involvement in FIDE governance or international chess administration as of September 2026.
No public campaign-finance disclosure establishes that Jan Henric Buettner personally funded increased prize funds for FIDE events as of September 2026.
Malcolm Pein has longstanding relationships with national chess federations through decades of organizing international chess events.
Jan Henric Buettner publicly withdrew from the FIDE presidential race in September 2025.
Direct campaign financing reduces a ticket's dependence on donors whose interests could deter FIDE member federations.
Incumbent administration support does not identify whether Arkady Dvorkovich was a candidate on a competing ticket in the 2026 election.
FIDE presidential elections are decided by one vote from each member federation, regardless of campaign spending within that federation.
FIDE's 2026 presidential nomination deadline had not yet passed as of September 2026.
Timur Turlov chairs the Kazakhstan Chess Federation, a FIDE member federation, as of 2026.
Incumbent officeholders running for re-election win a large share of contested elections across many organizations.
Incumbent officeholders in FIDE presidential elections have historically won re-election when seeking another term.
National federation delegates in FIDE presidential elections often favor tickets featuring candidates with strong playing credentials and international stature.

FIDE presidential elections are decided by votes from national federation delegates rather than by direct votes from chess players or the public, so Anand's fame among the general chess-playing population does not translate into delegate votes.
National chess federation delegates cast the votes that determine the winner of FIDE presidential elections.
Federation officials' personal familiarity with an organizer does not necessarily translate into votes for the ticket that organizer joins in the 2026 FIDE election.
Jan Henric Buettner announced his withdrawal in a public statement posted on his X (Twitter) account on September 22, 2025.
Jan Henric Buettner submitted official candidacy paperwork for the FIDE presidential ticket with Malcolm Pein for the 2026 election.
In every FIDE presidential election since 2010, at least one additional ticket beyond the initially prominent contenders registered before the candidacy deadline.
Several national chess federations expressed dissatisfaction with Arkady Dvorkovich's handling of FIDE finances and sanctions policy between 2022 and 2026.
FIDE requires a presidential candidate to secure nominations from at least ten national federations to appear on the 2026 election ballot.
Timur Turlov has publicly criticized FIDE's financial management and transparency under Arkady Dvorkovich's leadership prior to the 2026 election.
FIDE presidential elections require nomination endorsement from at least five national federations, which favors candidates with established federation coalitions over newly formed tickets.
Support from most national federations in the 2022 FIDE election does not establish those federations’ voting intentions for the 2026 election.
A vice-presidential candidate’s playing prestige does not measure a presidential candidate’s ability to secure commitments from national federation delegates.
Longstanding professional relationships give Malcolm Pein direct channels for presenting the ticket's platform to national chess federation delegates.
National federation delegates select tickets partly on policy commitments and geopolitical alliances rather than longstanding organizational relationships.
Wadim Rosenstein's 2026 campaign recruited former FIDE chief executive Emil Sutovsky as its candidate for deputy president.
Timur Turlov's Freedom Holding Corp. operates across Europe and Central Asia, regions represented by numerous voting FIDE member federations.
Viswanathan Anand's service as FIDE Deputy President since 2022 associates the ticket with the administration that Timur Turlov publicly criticizes.
FIDE presidential and vice-presidential candidates typically require established credibility with national federation delegates who cast the electing votes.
FIDE presidential candidates are frequently chosen for financial backing or political connections rather than prior governance experience.
Arkady Dvorkovich is not affiliated with the Buettner/Pein, Rosenstein/Tang, or Turlov/Anand tickets in the 2026 FIDE presidential election.
National federation delegates from Asian countries with prior ties to Gordon Tang are more likely to vote for a ticket he is on in FIDE presidential elections.
Network relationships with Asian federation officials do not necessarily translate into their votes for a specific ticket in the 2026 FIDE election.
Gordon Tang's public business biography lists directorships in real estate and finance companies but no role in any national chess federation or FIDE committee before 2026.
Gordon Tang has served as a national chess federation official or delegate to FIDE congresses prior to 2026.
A new ticket registering before the 2026 FIDE candidacy deadline could go on to win the election rather than merely appear on the ballot.
Additional tickets that registered in past elections since 2010 lost to one of the initially prominent contenders in nearly every case.
The Turlov-Anand ticket was formed for the first time in 2025 or 2026 without a pre-existing coalition of national federation endorsements.
Timur Turlov and Viswanathan Anand have secured endorsement nominations from at least five national chess federations for the 2026 FIDE presidential election.
Chess news outlets including Chess.com reported on September 22, 2025 that Jan Henric Buettner posted his withdrawal statement on X.
Jan Henric Buettner announced his withdrawal from the FIDE presidential race through a formal press release distributed via FIDE-affiliated news channels rather than a personal X post.
FIDE member federations elect the president–deputy president ticket as a joint slate rather than evaluating only the presidential candidate.
Arkady Dvorkovich would head a fourth ticket if he sought re-election in the 2026 FIDE presidential election.
Not publicly ruling out a 2026 candidacy does not establish that Arkady Dvorkovich will contest the 2026 FIDE presidential election.
FIDE presidential elections give each participating member federation one vote, allowing coordinated regional blocs to affect the result substantially.
Asian national chess federations constitute only a minority of the national federations eligible to vote in FIDE presidential elections.
National federations in countries where Freedom Holding Corp. operates may be more inclined to vote for a candidate with regional business ties.
FIDE presidential elections are decided by one vote per national federation regardless of the federation's regional business ties to any candidate.
Gordon Tang participated in FIDE-sponsored chess events before September 2026 in an official organizational or financial capacity.
Registration frequency does not establish the electoral support of any additional ticket.
The five-federation nomination requirement determines ballot eligibility rather than electoral support among voting national federations.
Timur Turlov's Kazakhstan Chess Federation and Viswanathan Anand's standing with the All India Chess Federation each carry preexisting relationships with multiple national federations.
Timur Turlov and Viswanathan Anand each retain extensive personal contacts within national chess federations built over prior decades of chess administration and play.
Chess.com’s September 22, 2025 report does not independently verify that the cited X account belonged to Jan Henric Buettner.
Gordon Tang's Singapore-based business, Sun Cable, and philanthropic ventures involved partnerships with organizations in China, India, and Singapore before 2026.
Most Asian national chess federation votes in FIDE presidential elections have historically been coordinated through the Asian Chess Federation rather than individual business relationships.
Freedom Holding Corp.'s commercial presence does not establish organizational relationships with the national chess federations operating in the same countries.
